newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean civil aviation incidents.
newsitem.headline: South Korean civil aviation incidents.

text.p: The following is a chronology of major South Korean civil aviation incidents:
Feb 26, 1958 -- Six hijackers commandeered South Korean government airliner with 26 people aboard to North Korea. No casualties reported.
Dec 11, 1969 -- A Korean Air Lines (KAL) aircraft carrying 47 passengers and crew on internal flight hijacked to North Korea.
Jan 23, 1971 -- Two killed and 12 injured when a would-be hijacker opened fire on a domestic flight.
August 2, 1976 -- A KAL cargo plane crashed on landing in Tehran. Five crew killed.
April 20, 1978 -- A KAL airliner forced to land in Russian Far East by Soviet fighters. Two killed and 10 wounded when MiGs opened fire.
Nov 19, 1980 -- A KAL Boeing 747 belly-landed at Seoul's Kimpo Airport and caught fire, killing 15 of the 206 people aboard.
Sept 15, 1981 -- KAL Boeing 747 missed runway at Manila airport due to engine problem. Twelve injured.
Sept 1, 1983 -- KAL flight 007 from New York to Seoul shot down by Soviet fighter over Sakhalin. All 269 on board died.
Dec 13, 1983 -- KAL cargo plane attempting take-off from wrong runway at Anchorage smashed into waiting commuter plane. Six people injured.
Nov 29, 1987 -- North Korean agent blows up KAL Boeing 707-858 over Burma, killing all 115 passengers.
July 27, 1989 -- KAL DC-10 carrying 199 people crashed near fog-bound Tripoli airport killing 72 people and injuring 70.
July 26, 1993 -- Asiana Boeing 737-500 carrying 110 passengers and crew crashed in the southwest of the Korean peninsula. killing 66.
